title: Life & Annuities
meta_description: How Dataq Software engineers life and annuity operations: straight-through underwriting evidence factories, servicing modernization across decades of records, LDTI and IFRS 17 valuation pipelines, death-claim and contestability assembly, lapse analytics and illustration governance — built against your admin core and actuarial estate.

blocks.x: Life and annuity books run on the longest promises in financial services: underwriting decisions made in weeks that stand for thirty years, servicing relationships measured in decades, and reserves that must survive accounting regime changes (LDTI, IFRS 17) that rewrite the arithmetic without changing the risk. The machinery behind those promises is document-heavy and decision-dense — applications, attending physician statements, contestability files, valuation extracts, lapse curves — which makes it ideal ground for governed automation, and equally dangerous ground for ungoverned experiments. This page is the engineering picture of the life insurer's machine as Dataq Software sees it: what runs from new business to runoff, where each stage leaks money or invites findings, and the six deep builds that move case cycle time, valuation effort and servicing cost with the evidence a regulator or auditor will ask for.
How a life book actually runs

In life and annuities, the promise is manufactured in the new business engine, and the engine is a document conveyor. An application arrives through an illustration platform or an agent's point-of-sale tool; the requirements engine orders paramedical exams, MIB checks, prescription histories, motor vehicle reports and attending physician statements; tele-underwriting calls capture the health interview as structured notes. Every document is a file to classify, extract and reconcile against the application's declarations. Financial underwriting adds tax forms and net-worth evidence. Only when the evidence file is complete does the underwriting decision — approve, rate, decline, or refer to a reinsurer — become possible, and the clock has been running the whole time.

Issue is the beginning of a thirty-year servicing relationship, and the policy administration core becomes the system of record for everything: premium collection and grace periods, address and beneficiary changes, surrenders and policy loans, annuity roll-ins, rider elections and guaranteed lifetime withdrawal benefit behaviour. Servicing transactions are individually small and collectively enormous — a block of a million policies generates hundreds of thousands of transactions a year, each one a document-and-verification workflow inside a core built when transactions were batch. Death claims open a different file: contestability-period analysis, medical evidence, beneficiary identification and payment — the moment the entire book's credibility is tested in public.

Underneath, the actuarial engine converts the book into numbers the balance sheet can trust. Valuation extracts are assembled from the admin core into cohorts for LDTI and IFRS 17 measurement; assumptions are monitored against experience studies; lapse and mortality behaviour feed pricing, reserving and in-force reinsurance negotiations. Every quarter the same data travels the same path, and where the path is manual, the quarter is consumed by preparation rather than judgment. The quiet truth of this sub-industry is that the actuarial output is only as good as the least-governed extract feeding it — which is usually a spreadsheet held by someone who might retire.
The estate underneath: systems this work touches

Programs here succeed or fail on how honestly the estate is mapped before anything is built. Dataq Software starts every life engagement by naming the systems, their owners, their change cadences and their data contracts — and in this sub-industry the map must include document archives and vendor evidence feeds, because the decisions that matter run on evidence those systems hold. blocks.x: Where the margin leaks

Ask life and annuity operations and actuarial leaders where the money leaks and the answers converge on the same eight places, described in their own words. Dataq Software scores each of them in your estate during the diagnostic, because the leak that dominates a career book is often minor on a digital-national book — and vice versa.

items: Underwriting evidence assembled by hand

APS records arrive as faxes and portal dumps; paramedical, MIB and prescription results land in separate queues; case managers spend their hours collecting instead of deciding. Every day of evidence chase is a day of consumer abandonment risk — and the fintech-era competitors quote in minutes what a legacy chain quotes in weeks.
A straight-through ceiling set by documents

STP rates plateau well below their potential because the automation that exists reads only the structured application, not the evidence file underneath it. The cases that would auto-approve if the machine could read the APS keep landing on underwriter desks with everything else already resolved.
Valuation data wrangling every quarter

LDTI and IFRS 17 turned valuation data into a standing obligation, and most carriers meet it with extract-and-reconcile spreadsheets. Preparation consumes the actuarial quarter, assumption changes hide in documents, and restatements surface at the worst possible moment — audit.
Servicing queues with abandonment risk

Surrender, loan and beneficiary-change requests route through document-heavy verification queues. Callers abandon, complaints escalate, and the cost per transaction of a block built for batch processing carries the expense ratio of the whole book.
Lapse signals arriving too late to act

Payment behaviour, engagement and life-event signals exist in the estate, but they reach a retention decision after the grace period has expired. Save campaigns fire on stale lists, and in-force value leaks through a window the models could have seen weeks earlier.
Death claims that test the brand

Contestability analysis, evidence collection and beneficiary identification run as manual workflows with clocks tracked in spreadsheets. Cycle time becomes a complaint, complaints become regulator conversations, and the file that finally pays cannot always show why it took as long as it did.
In-force reinsurance flying blind

Ceded reporting lags the book, requirement mismatches surface at claim rather than at issue, and recoverables reconcile slowly or not at all. The treaty that was priced on one portfolio is silently servicing another, and nobody notices until a large claim tests the notification window.
Suitability and illustration evidence scattered

Illustrations are generated by governed engines, but the evidence around them — suitability grounds, replacement tracking, disclosure delivery — lives in agent files and state-dependent processes. Exams reconstruct it by request; conduct analytics see nothing until a pattern is already public.

blocks.x: The pattern across all eight leaks is the same: decisions are made at the end of a document conveyor nobody has industrialised. In life books the conveyor is longer than anywhere else in insurance — which is why the first build is almost always evidence assembly, not a smarter decision model.
How Dataq Software works life and annuities

Dataq Software builds inside the estate you already run — the admin core, the new business workflow, the valuation stack, the claims platform — not against them. We do not arrive with a replacement admin system or a strategy deck that ends where the hard part begins. The engagement model is engineering-first: a two-week diagnostic that baselines one workflow end to end — new business evidence, valuation preparation, servicing transactions or death claims — then a scoped build that ships behind your change process, your model-risk framework and your privacy controls from the first sprint.

Three engineering commitments shape everything we deliver in this sub-industry. First, every automated decision carries replay: underwriting inputs, model versions, rating plans and reason codes are stored, so an adverse-underwriting question or a claims dispute twelve years later is a query, not an archaeology project on an archive. Second, every generative component is permission-aware and citation-bound — grounded in your policy contract, underwriting manual and product terms, never the open internet, with health data scoped to the case. Third, every build lands with its evidence layer: the artifacts a market-conduct examiner, statutory auditor or valuation reviewer will ask for are generated continuously by the system.

The commercial model follows the same logic: where the metric is clean we contract against the delta with the baseline locked during the diagnostic, and where it is confounded the feasibility read says so. The published record behind this approach sits exactly on this ground — a leading North American life insurer assembled underwriting evidence in hours with case cycle time down 44% in Dataq Software's record — because the evidence factory is where document-heavy books pay first.
The builds: six deep engineering services for life and annuities

The catalog below is the whole of our life and annuities practice. Each build is named for the workflow it changes, sized in the diagnostic, and shipped with the controls its regulator will expect. None of them require replacing the admin core; every one of them requires taking the evidence contracts seriously — because in this sub-industry the evidence is the product.
1. New business and straight-through underwriting — the evidence factory

The build industrialises the document conveyor that sets your case cycle time. A requirements gateway orders and receives paramedical results, MIB checks, prescription histories, motor vehicle reports and APS packages; document intelligence classifies every incoming record, extracts the clinical facts with confidence scores, and reconciles them against the application's declarations. Tele-underwriting notes are structured at capture. The evidence file assembles itself, flags the contradictions a human must resolve, and presents the underwriter — when one is needed — with a complete, cited case instead of a folder.

The decision layer then raises the STP ceiling: clean cases with coherent evidence flow straight through rules and models to issue, rated cases carry their debits and reason codes automatically, and referrals to in-force reinsurers are flagged early — with the reinsurer's specific requirements attached — instead of surfacing at claim. Every decision writes to the replay store, so an adverse-underwriting question years later is answered from the record the decision made. In the published record, this build took a leading North American life insurer's case cycle time down 44%, with evidence assembly absorbed by agents under human checkpoints.
2. Policy servicing and admin modernization — decades of records, one clean surface

The servicing build extracts the transaction layer from the admin core using a strangler pattern: surrenders, loans, beneficiary changes, address updates, rider elections and annuity roll-ins execute through a governed decision layer that validates, verifies and writes back through the core's own interfaces. Change-data-capture streams the core's activity into the lakehouse, so every transaction carries its context — prior transactions, documents, verification evidence — instead of a queue number. Migrated blocks are mapped into one conformed policy master with survivorship rules your data owners sign.

The queue work — verification, document assembly, escalations — moves to agentic workers under explicit role scopes, with human checkpoints on anything that touches money or beneficiaries. Cycle-time telemetry shows where each transaction spends its hours, abandonment is measured at the funnel rather than guessed, and product-change velocity improves because the transaction layer is no longer a release negotiation. The measurable deltas are transaction cycle time, cost per transaction and the servicing abandonment that currently compounds quietly.
3. The actuarial valuation pipeline — LDTI and IFRS 17 without the wrangling

The valuation build is a governed pipeline from the admin core into the actuarial stack: policy-level extracts assembled into cohorts with the aggregation discipline LDTI and IFRS 17 demand, assumption sets versioned and traceable, discount-rate inputs governed, and reconciliation to the general ledger running as a monitored query instead of a month-end ritual. Experience studies assemble from the same marts — mortality, lapse, utilisation — so the assumptions that drive the valuation are watched by the same machinery that feeds them.

Actuaries stay in command: the pipeline moves data, not judgment, and every number answers the audit question — where did this come from — as a lineage query into the lakehouse. Disclosure datasets are validated before they leave, assumption monitoring flags experience drift between valuations instead of at them, and restatement risk drops because the cohort logic is code rather than a spreadsheet convention. The measurable deltas are valuation preparation effort, restatement count and the hours audit evidence currently costs each reporting period.
4. Death claims and beneficiary service — the contestability file, assembled

The death-claim build treats the claim as the evidence problem it is. Intake captures the notification and the beneficiaries; the pipeline assembles the file automatically — the application, the policy contract, contestability and misstatement windows computed precisely from issue dates, MIB checks where permitted, medical records, coroner and autopsy reports — and presents the examiner with a complete, cited case. Contestability analysis is supported by the dates and the evidence rather than by a manual calendar calculation, and beneficiary communications are generated grounded in the contract language.

The guardrails are deliberate: investigation decisions stay with human examiners; state unfair-claims clocks are tracked per case, not per spreadsheet; fraud signals — policy churn patterns, agent-linked anomalies, suspicious timing — route to a SIU-equivalent workbench with their rationale attached. Payment, escheatment and reinsurance notification follow the same evidence chain, so the file that closes shows exactly why it took the time it took. The measurable deltas are claim cycle time, documentation completeness and the complaint rate that follows from both.
5. In-force analytics and lapse decisioning — the book as a live asset

The in-force build makes the book legible to itself. Change-data-capture streams payment behaviour, engagement events and transaction history into the lakehouse; lapse propensity models score the block continuously with an action policy attached — payment retries, engagement treatments, repricing windows — so the decision arrives inside the retention window instead of after the grace period. GLWB rider behaviour is monitored against the withdrawal assumptions, and experience signals flow to pricing and in-force reinsurance negotiations on time, with the evidence attached.

Treatments are governed like the decisions they are: every retention action is logged with its inputs, vulnerable-customer constraints are hard rules the optimizer cannot violate, and save campaigns are measured against held-out controls because this is one of the few places in a life book where a clean experiment is cheap. The measurable deltas are save rate, lapse ratio movement and the retention campaign economics the finance function currently reconstructs from marketing spreadsheets.
6. Illustration, suitability and point-of-sale governance

Illustration engines produce compliant outputs; the governance around them is where exam findings live. The build wraps the point-of-sale flow in an evidence layer: every illustration is checked against the currently approved scales before it reaches a customer, suitability grounds are captured as structured evidence rather than checkboxes, replacement analysis runs with prior-policy data assembled automatically, and disclosure delivery is tracked to the document. The chain from illustration to issued policy becomes a single auditable record.

The guardrails encode the regulatory reality: state advertising and illustration rules as versioned policy-as-code, replacement and best-interest evidence assembled per sale, and agent conduct analytics that watch the pattern — churn-adjacent replacements, illustrative-rate outliers — before an exam does. Every sale file answers the conduct question as a query, so a market-conduct request is a retrieval rather than a reconstruction. The measurable deltas are suitability evidence completeness, replacement-related complaints and the preparation time exams currently cost.

blocks.note: Lanes and nodes are named for the systems a life build actually touches — the admin core, the claims platform, the illustration engine, the requirements gateway — not a generic stack. The hot nodes are where program differentiation concentrates: the permission-aware retrieval index over decades of policy documents, and the STP underwriting decision service that turns assembled evidence into issued contracts.

blocks.x: The data plane: from migrated blocks to a governed policy history

Every decision gap in a life book traces back to a data gap, and the gaps here have a distinctive shape: history is long, formats are many, and the evidence that matters is mostly documents. The data plane build handles both. The admin core, claims platform and payment streams land through change-data-capture into a governed lakehouse in near real time, while the document archive — applications, APS packages, contract files, claim correspondence — is digitized, classified and indexed against the policy so that thirty-year-old evidence becomes retrievable, not mythical.

Governance is engineered, not asserted. Every feed carries a schema contract with a named owner, a freshness SLA and a reconciliation check against the source system's own controls. The conformed policy and insured masters apply survivorship rules across migrated blocks with the duplicate-suspect queue surfaced rather than hidden, and every downstream consumer — underwriting features, lapse models, valuation extracts, claims assembly — reads through the contract layer, so a schema change fails loudly at the contract instead of silently inside a valuation. The reconciliation ritual that eats the first week of every quarter becomes a monitored query.

items: Streaming admin and payment ingestion
change-data-capture from policy administration and premium events with exactly-once semantics, keeping lapse and servicing decisions current without touching the finance batch
Document archive digitization
decades of policy, evidence and claim documents classified, extracted and indexed per contract, so contestability and underwriting history answer as queries
Conformed policy and insured masters
survivorship and source-precedence rules signed off by data owners across migrated blocks, with duplicates surfaced rather than hidden
Feature store discipline
one definition of payment behaviour, engagement recency and claim history shared by underwriting, lapse and servicing — the end of two teams computing the same feature differently

blocks.x: The decision layer: underwriting, replay and reason codes

A life book runs on decisions with the longest legal tails in insurance: an underwriting decision stands for decades, a lapse treatment carries conduct duties, a claims decision faces beneficiaries, courts and regulators. The decision layer we build treats those tails as first-class requirements. Every decision records its inputs, evidence citations, model versions, rating plans and reason codes in a replay store built for a horizon measured in decades, not quarters. When a policyholder dispute, a conduct exam or an internal audit asks why, the answer is retrieved from the record the decision made — not reconstructed from what someone remembers.

Champion/challenger governance is built in rather than bolted on: underwriting and lapse challengers run on shadow traffic with performance tracked in the registry your model-risk function owns, promotions pass through the gates your framework already defines, and rollbacks are rehearsed rather than improvised. The same decision layer hosts STP underwriting, lapse and retention treatments, claims triage and servicing verification, so the governance surface is one registry and one replay store — instead of four platforms with four audit stories and four explanations of the same evidence.
The agentic layer: digital workers with audit trails

The backlog work in a life book — evidence assembly, verification, valuation data preparation, claims file collation — follows patterns an agentic workforce can absorb without touching judgment authority. Dataq Software's agent platform runs digital workers with explicit role scopes: the tools they may call, the systems they may read, the actions that require a human checkpoint and the budget of work per run. Every run logs its steps, tool calls and outputs to the same evidence store the human workflow uses, so an agent's file is auditable exactly like a case manager's.

Where generative agents add leverage — summarising APS packages for an underwriter, drafting servicing verification summaries, assembling valuation extracts — the pattern is grounded generation with citation obligations and human authorship of record. Agents never issue policies, never move money, never change beneficiary records, and never alter a coded health fact; they move the work to the decision point and stop. The capacity story is measured in cleared cases per analyst per day, which is how new business and operations leaders who sponsor these programs justify them upward.
Controls and evidence: audit as a query

The regulatory surface of life and annuities is dense and unusually long-horizon: accounting regimes that rewrite measurement mid-contract, state conduct and advertising rules, suitability and best-interest standards, AML duties on premium channels, and privacy obligations over health data the book must retain for decades. Dataq Software's answer is the evidence layer — the artifacts a reviewer will ask for are generated continuously by the systems themselves. blocks.x: Integration engineering: the estate stays, the contracts change

Life estates are the most layered in insurance, and the fastest way to fail a program is to promise greenfield. Our integration posture is contractual: we define schema contracts with each system owner, land data through CDC and governed APIs, write back through the admin and claims interfaces your change process already controls, and keep every new component independently deployable behind feature flags. The admin core is not replaced; it is supplied with better context and drained of the decision and verification work it was never good at.

The vendor chain gets the same treatment. Requirements vendors, MIB, prescription databases, tele-underwriting platforms and reinsurance administration systems sit behind an abstraction layer with contract tests, so a vendor swap is a configuration change with a migration runbook rather than a re-platform. Where a legacy admin or mainframe component must stay, the offload pattern applies: the batch cycle keeps posting, while the decision surfaces read from the stream the offload produces. This is unglamorous work, and it is the reason the builds above hold up in production instead of in a pilot.

blocks.x: The team and the operating rhythm

A life build team is small and senior: a lead engineer who has run decision systems in regulated insurance, data engineers who own the CDC and contract layer, ML engineers who own scoring and evaluation, a controls engineer who owns the evidence layer, and a domain lead who has run new business desks, valuation cycles or claims operations in production estates. Agentic-workflow specialists join for the evidence-assembly builds, and a clinical or underwriting SME reviews the health-data boundaries. The team works to your release calendar and your gate vocabulary from the first week.

The rhythm is the same at every client: weekly operations review on the workflow's own telemetry, fortnightly gate submissions to change and model-risk, quarterly challenger reviews aligned to the valuation calendar, and an incident practice that treats the replay store and the evidence layer as production-critical systems — because by the second quarter, they are. Escalations go to named engineers, not to a queue.
Failure modes we design against

Programs like these fail in known ways, and in life books the failure modes have a horizon problem: decisions that stand for decades make documentation debt more expensive than anywhere else. We name them in the feasibility read and design against them explicitly, because a program that cannot survive its second quarter is not worth starting.

blocks.x: Questions life and annuity leaders ask us

items: Do we need to replace our admin core first?

No. None of the six builds require a core replacement. They consume streams from the admin and claims estate and write back through your interfaces. The core stays; it stops being the bottleneck for decisions and verification.
How does this pass model risk and actuarial review?

Every scoring and generative component ships with its documentation: data lineage, evaluation results against golden sets, guardrail inventory and drift monitoring. The actuarial function stays in command of assumptions and judgment; the machinery moves data, not conclusions.
Will underwriters and case managers lose their work?

The builds move evidence collection and verification to agents and put judgment back in human hands with complete, cited files. Capacity is redeployed to the complex cases the backlog currently neglects; programs are justified in cleared cases per analyst, not headcount removed.
How do you handle health data across a thirty-year book?

Health evidence is scoped per case, access is logged with purpose, retention is enforced as a pipeline property, and the archive is digitized under the same controls. Data-subject questions answer as joins across the conformed policy master.
Can the valuation build coexist with our audit calendar?

Yes — it is designed around it. The pipeline lands before the cycle it must support, reconciliation to the ledger runs as a monitored query, and parallel-run equivalence is demonstrated on a real reporting period before the old process retires.
What is the smallest program worth running?

One workflow, one baseline, one vertical slice — new business evidence and valuation preparation are the two most common starters because their clocks and queues are already instrumented. If the diagnostic cannot find the delta, we say so and stop.
How do the agents avoid becoming shadow AI?

Agents run inside the governed platform with role scopes, tool allow-lists, human checkpoints and full run logs. They never issue, pay or change beneficiary records. The shadow-AI failure mode is what happens without those controls; the program's goal is to eliminate the conditions that create it.
Who owns the build after you leave?

Your teams, with the runbooks, contracts, evaluation suites and registry entries transferred as gate conditions during expansion — not as a closing deliverable. Several programs run entirely in-house after the second quarter.
